title: Understanding and monitoring renal microvascular remodeling in CKD by super-resolution ultrasound
summary:
Microbubbles have been developed as contrast-agents for ultrasound in order to visualize blood perfusion. It is in clinical use in order to better visualize blood vessels in liver or kidney in ultrasound. 
We have developed a high-resolution contrast enhanced ultrasound method called motion-model ultrasound localization microscopy (mULM), which allows for post-processing of ultrasound video sequences thanks to microbubbles and is able to visualize even smaller blood vessels than before. 
We want to test, if this method is of use in kidney diagnostics. Getting a better visualisation of kidney microcirculation could help to detect kidney fibrosis in earlier stages or to better judge disease severity and to predict progression. 
We have already shown that mULM can improve blood vessel visualization in a patient with kidney transplantation. Our aim is to improve mULM for use in kidney disease diagnostics clinically. The study uses clinically generated images after pseudonymisation for post-processing and correlates imaging results with clinical data and disease progression.

interventions.name: Patients after kidney transplantation (eGFR >20ml/min): Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound
Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD): Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients after kidney transplantation with GFR ≥ 20 ml/min (Study part A)
2. Patients with CKD with GFR ≥ 20 ml/min  (Study part B)
3. Written consent
4. Patients who are contractually capable and able to follow the requests of the study staff
Exclusion criteria:
1. minors
2. allergy against ultrasound contrast agent or components sulfur hexafluoride, macrogol 4000, Colfoscerilstearat, 1-(1,2-Dipalmitoyl-3-sn-phosphatidyl)glycerol-Natriumsalt Palmitic acid
3. Left-right -shunt
4. signs of cardiovascular instability such as acute coronary syndrome, clinically instable ischemic heart disease, acute myocardial infarction, angina pectoris within 7 days prior, recent coronary intervention (PTA with or without stent), acute cardiac failure, cardiac insufficiency NYHA III or IV, severe arrhythmias
5. acute endocarditis
6. artificial heart valves
7. acute systemic inflammation and/or sepsis
8. coagulopathy or recent thromboembolic event
9. liver or kidney disease in end stage
10. severe pulmonary hypertension (pA pressure >90mmHg)
11. uncontrolled systemic hypertension
12. acute respiratory distress syndrome
13. clinically significant pulmonary disease including severe COPD
14. pregnancy
15. persons under official directive (prisoners, e.g.)
16. persons who are working for the sponsor or are dependent of the sponsor
17. alcohol or drug misuse
18. expected non-compliance
